backlog.spec: Replace the 2048-bit binary Morgan fingerprint with a count-based Morgan fingerprint (GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy, radius 2, fpSize 1024). Keep the descriptors and the rest of the ensemble unchanged.
backlog.title: Add count-based Morgan features with smaller size

backlog.spec: Change the LGBMClassifier call to learning_rate=0.02, n_estimators=800, num_leaves=31, min_child_samples=10, subsample=0.8, subsample_freq=1, colsample_bytree=0.3, reg_lambda=1.0. Keep random_state=seed. Slower shrinkage with more trees and row bagging usually improves generalization on small datasets. Verify the job still fits inside the time limit; if fit time is high, keep n_estimators=800 and set n_jobs=8.
backlog.title: Retuned LightGBM with slower learning rate and row subsampling

backlog.spec: Append a small set of counts per molecule: number of chiral centres (Chem.FindMolChiralCenters with includeUnassigned=True), number of stereo double bonds (bonds with stereo not STEREONONE), number of triple bonds, number of amide bonds (C(=O)N pattern via Chem.MolFromSmarts), number of ester bonds, number of sulfonyl groups, and number of halogen atoms. Concatenate these after the existing descriptor block, clip to training 1st/99th percentiles, and leave the RF and LightGBM blend and their hyperparameters unchanged.
backlog.title: Stereochemistry and bond-type count features

backlog.spec: The current LGBM settings (300 trees, lr 0.05, 15 leaves, colsample 0.3) are untuned. Replace with a configuration regularised for ~1300 training rows and ~2300 columns: n_estimators=900, learning_rate=0.02, num_leaves=7, min_child_samples=10, colsample_bytree=0.15, subsample=0.8, subsample_freq=1, reg_lambda=5.0, max_bin=127, random_state=seed, n_jobs=8, verbose=-1. Keep the RF and the rank averaging unchanged. More, smaller, more heavily feature-subsampled trees usually transfer better to held-out scaffolds than fewer deeper ones.
backlog.title: Tune LightGBM for the small, wide, scaffold-split regime

backlog.spec: In featurize(), append the 167-bit MACCS keys fingerprint to each row: rdMolDescriptors.GetMACCSKeysFingerprint(mol) converted with np.array(list(fp), dtype=np.float32) (or via DataStructs.ConvertToNumpyArray). Concatenate it after the Morgan bits and before the descriptors. MACCS keys encode hand-curated pharmacophore and functional-group patterns that are informative for membrane permeation and generalize across scaffolds. Everything else stays the same.
backlog.title: Add MACCS keys to the feature matrix

backlog.spec: Replace the single LightGBM member with three LightGBM classifiers, each trained on a different random 60% column subset of the full feature matrix (sampled with a seed-derived RandomState and fixed per member), using the same learning rate, leaves and tree count as now. Average their predict_proba values on the test rows before the rank transform. This is a simple feature-bagging ensemble on the existing feature matrix, with no new features and no change to the RF member.
backlog.title: Fold-wise LightGBM bagging on descriptor subsets

backlog.spec: Change the LGBM to n_estimators=600, learning_rate=0.02, num_leaves=8, min_child_samples=20, subsample=0.8 with subsample_freq=1, colsample_bytree=0.2, reg_lambda=5. Aim for smoother generalization to unseen scaffolds.
backlog.title: Stronger LGBM regularization

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, after featurizing, keep only the Morgan bit columns (the first N_BITS columns) whose training-fold prevalence is between 1% and 99% and whose chi-square association with train_y is in the top 256 among those bits. Always keep all descriptor columns. Apply the same column selection to test features before calling the RF and LightGBM members. Compute the selection from training data only so there is no leakage across folds. Cap the number of bits used to 256 and leave the blend and hyperparameters unchanged.
backlog.title: Per-fold univariate filter on fingerprint bits

backlog.spec: Add a small helper that returns eight graph-shape scalars per molecule using RDKit ring info and the molecular graph: size of the largest fused ring system (atoms in rings sharing at least one bond, merged transitively), number of fused ring systems, number of spiro atoms (rdMolDescriptors.CalcNumSpiroAtoms), number of bridgehead atoms (rdMolDescriptors.CalcNumBridgeheadAtoms), length of the longest acyclic carbon chain (via Chem.GetDistanceMatrix restricted to non-ring atoms, or a simple DFS), number of branch points (heavy atoms with degree >= 3 outside rings), molecular diameter from the topological distance matrix, and fraction of heavy atoms that are in rings. Append these to the existing descriptor block, clip to training 1st/99th percentiles, and leave the rest of fit_predict unchanged.
backlog.title: Ring-system and chain-shape descriptors

backlog.spec: Drop near-constant columns (variance under 1e-6 on train) and fingerprint bits that are on in fewer than 10 train molecules. Then train the RF and LGBM with 3 different seeds (seed, seed+1, seed+2) and average the ranks. This cuts noise and variance.
backlog.title: Seed-bagged ensemble with feature selection

backlog.spec: Add a linear model that sees the raw sparse fingerprint signal: train sklearn.linear_model.LogisticRegression(C=1.0, max_iter=3000, solver='liblinear') on the fingerprint+hand-descriptor block standardised with StandardScaler (fit on train only) and append its scaled_rank predictions to the ensemble. Final prediction is the mean of scaled_rank of RF, LGBM and the logistic model with weights 0.4, 0.4, 0.2. Linear models on high-dimensional binary fingerprints make errors that are decorrelated from trees, so even a weaker member can lower the rank-averaged loss.
backlog.title: Logistic regression on fingerprints as a linear ensemble member

backlog.spec: Replace the scaled_rank combination with a plain average of the two members' predicted probabilities: return 0.5 * (rf.predict_proba(X_test)[:, 1] + gb.predict_proba(X_test)[:, 1]), deleting the scaled_rank helper if nothing else uses it. Rank-averaging discards the members' confidence, flattening every fold's predictions to a uniform spread, which loses information whenever one model is sharply confident on a subset and near-chance elsewhere; AUROC is computed from the ordering of the averaged score, and a probability average can order borderline molecules differently from a rank average. This is a small, clean change that tests whether the rank step adopted early on is actually helping now that the feature set has changed substantially.
backlog.title: Average calibrated probabilities instead of ranks

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, before producing the final predictions, run a 3-fold GroupKFold over the training molecules grouped by Murcko scaffold (rdkit.Chem.Scaffolds.MurckoScaffold.MurckoScaffoldSmiles on each training SMILES, falling back to the SMILES itself if it returns an empty string). Collect out-of-fold scaled-rank predictions for both members, then pick the weight w from a small grid, e.g. 0.0 to 1.0 in steps of 0.1, that maximises roc_auc_score on the out-of-fold scores of w * rank_rf + (1 - w) * rank_gb. Refit both members on the whole training fold and combine the test ranks with the chosen w. This lets the blend adapt per fold rather than assuming 0.5 is right everywhere, and the inner split mirrors the scaffold-disjoint evaluation. Keep the inner CV to 3 folds and reuse the same seed so the job stays within the time budget.
backlog.title: Choose the blend weight by out-of-fold scaffold CV

backlog.spec: Append MACCS keys (rdkit.Chem.MACCSkeys.GenMACCSKeys converted to a numpy array) to the feature matrix, as a compact substructure representation that generalizes across scaffolds. Keep everything else the same.
backlog.title: Add MACCS keys and Estate features

backlog.spec: After building X_train, compute the number of training molecules where each column is non-zero (for fingerprint bits) or where the value differs from the column median (for descriptors). Keep only columns present in at least 3 training molecules (fingerprint bits) and drop descriptor columns with zero variance on the training fold. Apply the same column mask to X_test. This removes sparse noise features that dilute the random forest's feature subsampling and speeds up both fits, which matters because the job has a 10-minute cap for 15 fits.
backlog.title: Prune rare and constant features

backlog.spec: Pass class_weight='balanced_subsample' to the RandomForestClassifier and is_unbalance=True or class_weight='balanced' to the LGBMClassifier. Leave everything else unchanged.
backlog.title: Balanced class weights

backlog.spec: Make no functional change to train.py and run it as-is to obtain a third independent measurement of the current incumbent (RF + LightGBM rank-average on Morgan bits, 11 physchem descriptors and the clipped full descList). The two existing incumbent runs differ by about 0.01, roughly twice the stated fold-noise sd, so the baseline against which every candidate is judged is itself uncertain. A third run tightens that estimate and makes all future single-run deltas interpretable. If an edit is required for the slot to be valid, change only a comment line or re-assert an existing constant to its current value (for example restate N_TREES = 300) so that behaviour is bit-identical.
backlog.title: Replicate the incumbent unchanged

backlog.spec: Train a CatBoostClassifier (iterations 500, depth 6, learning_rate 0.05, random_seed=seed, thread_count=8, verbose=0) on the descriptor + fingerprint features and add its scaled rank to the average of RF and LGBM.
backlog.title: Add CatBoost model to ensemble

backlog.spec: Address class imbalance in the loss: pass class_weight='balanced_subsample' to RandomForestClassifier, and for LightGBM set scale_pos_weight to (number of negatives / number of positives) computed from train_y. Leave the rest of the pipeline unchanged. AUROC depends only on ranking, but reweighting changes which splits the trees favour and can help the minority class's ordering, which is often the weaker part of the ranking.
backlog.title: Class-balanced weighting for the tree models

backlog.spec: Add a CatBoostClassifier(iterations=500, learning_rate=0.05, depth=6, l2_leaf_reg=3, rsm=0.3, random_seed=seed, thread_count=8, verbose=0) trained on the same X_train/X_test matrix as the other models. Rank-average its test probabilities with the RF and LightGBM ranks (equal weights, one-third each). CatBoost's ordered boosting and symmetric trees usually give a well-calibrated, low-variance ranker on small tabular data and differ from LightGBM's leaf-wise growth. Watch the time budget.
backlog.title: CatBoost as a third gradient-boosting member

backlog.spec: Broaden the substructure representation by concatenating two extra fingerprint blocks in featurize: the RDKit topological fingerprint from rdFingerprintGenerator.GetRDKitFPGenerator(maxPath=6, fpSize=1024) and the 167-bit MACCS keys from rdMolDescriptors.GetMACCSKeysFingerprint (convert with np.array of the ToBitString or use DataStructs.ConvertToNumpyArray). The final per-molecule vector becomes Morgan(2048) + RDKitFP(1024) + MACCS(167) + the 11 hand descriptors, and the full descriptor block is still appended in fit_predict. Build the generators once at module level so they are not recreated per call. Leave the RF and LGBM hyperparameters unchanged.
backlog.title: Add RDKit and MACCS fingerprints alongside Morgan

backlog.spec: The full descList includes columns with extreme ranges and heavy right tails (molecular weight, Kappa and Chi indices, Ipc, charge sums), currently handled only by 1st/99th percentile clipping fitted on the training fold. After the existing clip, additionally apply a signed log transform, np.sign(v) * np.log1p(np.abs(v)), to the clipped descriptor columns before they are hstacked, for both train and test. Trees are invariant to monotone transforms of a single feature, but this compresses outlying rows so that percentile clipping is no longer the only thing preventing a handful of molecules from dominating split thresholds, and it makes the 11 hand descriptors and the descList block live on comparable scales. Apply the same transform to the 11 physchem descriptors appended in featurize.
backlog.title: Signed log transform of the descriptor block

backlog.spec: Keep both members and the scaled-rank combination, but replace the fixed 0.5/0.5 average with a weighted one controlled by a single module-level constant, e.g. W_RF = 0.6, returning W_RF * scaled_rank(rf_prob) + (1 - W_RF) * scaled_rank(gb_prob). Use 0.6 in favour of the random forest, since the forest handles the wide, heavily correlated descList block more stably than a 300-round LightGBM with colsample 0.3 on the same matrix. This is a one-line change that costs no extra runtime and exposes a knob that can be moved later. Nothing else in featurization, hyperparameters or seeding changes.
backlog.title: Unequal rank-blend weight for RF and LightGBM

backlog.spec: Append hashed count fingerprints from rdFingerprintGenerator.GetAtomPairGenerator (fpSize 1024) to the features, in addition to Morgan. This adds distance-aware information that may transfer better across scaffolds.
backlog.title: Add atom-pair and topological torsion count features

backlog.spec: Set RADIUS=1 and N_BITS=512 so the descriptors dominate the feature matrix and the fingerprint block gets smaller. Leave the models unchanged.
backlog.title: Radius-1 Morgan with 512 bits

backlog.spec: Change the LGBMClassifier to n_estimators=800, learning_rate=0.02, num_leaves=8, min_child_samples=15, subsample=0.8 with subsample_freq=1, colsample_bytree=0.2. Leave the RF unchanged.
backlog.title: LightGBM lower learning rate, more trees

backlog.spec: In featurize or a new helper, compute Gasteiger partial charges per molecule with rdkit.Chem.rdPartialCharges.ComputeGasteigerCharges(mol), reading each atom's '_GasteigerCharge' property (replace NaN and inf with 0). Append six scalars per molecule: maximum partial charge, minimum partial charge, the sum of positive charges, the sum of absolute negative charges, the charge range (max minus min), and the number of heavy atoms with |charge| > 0.2. Concatenate these to the existing descriptor block, apply the same 1st/99th-percentile clipping fit on the training fold, and keep the RF and LightGBM blend unchanged.
backlog.title: Gasteiger partial-charge descriptors

backlog.spec: Add a third model: a similarity-weighted k-nearest-neighbour classifier on binary Morgan fingerprints (radius 2, 2048 bits). For each test molecule compute Tanimoto similarity to all training molecules with DataStructs.BulkTanimotoSimilarity, take the k=10 most similar training molecules, and predict the sum of similarity-weighted labels divided by the sum of similarities (fall back to the training mean if all similarities are zero). Rank-average this prediction with the RF and LightGBM ranks using equal weights (one-third each). Nearest-neighbour similarity is a different inductive bias from trees and is robust to unseen scaffolds.
backlog.title: Tanimoto kNN ensemble member

backlog.spec: Keep the existing RF and LGBM models and their feature matrix exactly as they are, and add a third model: CatBoostClassifier(iterations=600, learning_rate=0.05, depth=6, rsm=0.2, l2_leaf_reg=3, random_seed=seed, thread_count=8, verbose=0, allow_writing_files=False) fitted on the same X_train, y. Change the final return to the equal-weight mean of scaled_rank applied to each of the three predicted probabilities. CatBoost on 2048+ dense float columns may be slow, so if the job approaches the 10 minute limit reduce iterations to 300 and set border_count=64. Rank averaging keeps the scales comparable, so no other change is needed.
backlog.title: CatBoost as a third ensemble member

backlog.spec: Append about eight dimensionless ratios computed from the existing descriptors and a few atom counts: TPSA divided by MolWt, TPSA divided by heavy-atom count, (HBD + HBA) divided by heavy-atom count, Crippen LogP divided by heavy-atom count, fraction of heavy atoms that are heteroatoms (N, O, S, halogens), fraction of heavy atoms that are aromatic, fraction of heavy atoms that are nitrogen, and rotatable bonds divided by heavy-atom count. Use a divide-by-max(denominator, 1) guard. Stack them after the clipped descriptor block, clip them to training 1st/99th percentiles, and keep the RF and LightGBM members as they are.
backlog.title: Derived ratio descriptors

memo: Helped: the RF+LightGBM blend (0.1194 vs baseline ~0.1361) and appending RDKit descriptors (11 physchem 0.1040; full descList 0.0944 and 0.0842, incumbent mean_adjusted 0.0893 over 2 runs). Descriptors drive the gain. Did not help: other fingerprint swaps or additions (atom-pair 0.0949, MACCS 0.0921, Morgan counts 0.0940, BRICS 0.0938), model swaps (XGBoost 0.1041, CatBoost 0.0950, ExtraTrees 0.0948, SVC 0.1255), LightGBM variants (DART 0.0967, regularized 0.0958, monotone 0.0942), and extra members like LR or MLP. Tanimoto kNN (0.0884), label spreading (0.0896), torsion counts (0.0902) and LR stacking (0.0900) were within noise. The two incumbent runs differ by about 0.01, twice the noise sd of ~0.0049, so single-run deltas under 0.01 are unreliable. Next: replicate the incumbent and the kNN variant to firm up the baseline. Tune blend weights and tree hyperparameters on the descriptors. Try fewer fingerprint bits. Avoid more fingerprint swaps, kernel models and model-family swaps.
